entries.change: `part_of` moved from NOT APPLICABLE to APPLICABLE.
entries.why: The ruling required grammar productions `part_directive`, `part_of_directive`, `part_clause` — the DART grammar's node names — so it could never be satisfied by the C++ grammar, and it denied a value the analyzer emits from `preproc_include`. The ONTOLOGY's own definition (src/ast/types.ts) is the directive that NAMES A PART (`part 'x.dart'` / `#include "x.h"`); the C++ lane emits a QUOTED include as `part_of` (contract-mandatory metadata.partRole, partFile/partPath/partSymbol, target = the part's module symbol) and an ANGLE include as `imports`, with one row per (kind, target) so the two facts cannot suppress each other. Pinned by fixtures cpp/imports-include-910 and cpp/part-of-quoted-include; the lane's part_of oracle measures 2,328 rows, 0 disagreements.

previousRuling.reason: C++'s file-inclusion construct is `#include`, which IS a module edge and is published as `imports`; there is no part-file directive that shares one scope without importing (the construct `part_of` exists to distinguish).
previousRuling.vocabularyRuling: extended value (Dart `part`/`part of`), NOT APPLICABLE to C++.

MEASURED on the 2-repo corpus, DEFAULT state: 2,863 owner facts of 35,605 member-leaf rows (2,859 bare implicit-this + 4 `this->`), 0 emitted on a non-`calls` row, 0 failing the census's independent re-check against the emitting file's symbols. entries.change: INSTRUMENT GAP (tracked, not fixed) -> CLOSED: the 4 rows were functional casts of standard typedefs; the calls path now applies the guard the instantiates path already had.
entries.why: The reconstruction corpus (validation/cpp-audit/corpus-manifest.json) supplied the rows the original ledger could not name: 4 residual `calls` edges, one per shape, in Rcpp/src/date.cpp:1290 (`(int_fast32_t)(…)`), duckdb/third_party/ska_sort/ska_sort.hpp:119 and :129 (`std::int32_t(…)`, `std::int64_t(…)`) and nlohmann-json docs/.../value__return_type.cpp:12 (`std::uint64_t(0)`). A standard typedef is a TYPE; [cstdint]/[cstddef] guarantee it denotes a value type, so a call naming one is a fabrication with no reading. The analyzer already declines the identical class on the `instantiates` path via CPP_NON_CLASS_STANDARD_TYPES (`new uint8_t[5]`); the calls path simply never consulted the set. Fix: calleeLeafNode returns null for a callee spelled as a non-class standard type. Evidence: fixture cpp/typedef-functional-cast (RED pre-fix; real-call control), mutant cpp/standard-typedef-cast-call (CAUGHT, 71/71 cpp mutants), targeted re-parse of the 4-row files = 0 residual, and the whole-population re-measurement that follows. Rows stay 4 in the wall ledger because that is the row count the original population measured; the DISPOSITION is what changed.
